competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight tone turned more defensive as U.S. Treasury yields fell sharply on safe-haven demand, even with Fed minutes and officials still stressing further hikes and AI-related inflation risk. Crude stayed bid on Middle East and Strait of Hormuz supply anxiety, with WTI near 83.2 and Brent near 92.0. Gold held near 3,685.5 while U.S. equities stayed firm—Nasdaq near 23,879 and the Dow near 49,097—with VIX at 24.6. ECB hawkish rhetoric intensified after Pereira cited significant rising inflation pressure; Japan reported core CPI at year highs and Governor Ueda remains open to tightening. Next up: Canadian retail sales today, then Australia CPI and U.S. GDP/PCE on 25 Nov; watch whether the yield drop extends and oil marks hold above recent ranges.

postmortems.expression_assessment: AUDUSD was a weak pro-growth sleeve because the pair fell from 0.68 to 0.67 and the stated invalidation, a further downside break while SOFR March 2027 settled up, fired together.

causal.original_belief: A long in AUDUSD from 0.68 would gain if underappreciated global growth pulled that pro-cyclical currency higher.
causal.observed_reality: AUDUSD was closed on 19 November at 0.67 after a further downside break, and SOFR March 2027 settled up on the same episode.
causal.assumptions_right: The invalidation was correctly tied to a further downside break in AUDUSD occurring together with a higher SOFR March 2027 settle, and that combination ended the trade.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The view underweighted the chance that a higher SOFR March settle would dominate AUDUSD, so pro-growth resilience did not show up in that pair.
causal.causal_divergence: AUDUSD fell from 0.68 to 0.67 instead of rising, and the decline lined up with SOFR March 2027 settling up.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same growth view and the same higher SOFR March settle, expressing the view somewhere other than AUDUSD would have avoided the move from 0.68 to 0.67.
causal.future_implication: When SOFR March is settling higher, a pro-growth view belongs in a currency whose defensive cheapness is extreme or in the rate itself, rather than in a cyclical dollar pair that is breaking down.

postmortems.no_new_lesson: The loss from 0.68 to 0.67 is bounded variance around a stop that fired on its stated condition, a further AUDUSD downside break with SOFR March 2027 settling up, so the process remains sound.

postmortems.expression_assessment: SOFR September 2027 was a sound rates sleeve for a growth-and-hikes view, because the long rose from 4.71 to 4.74 and was closed with that gain realized.

causal.original_belief: A long in September 2027 SOFR from 4.71 would gain if a Fed still willing to discuss further hikes pulled that implied rate higher.
causal.observed_reality: The long was closed on 19 November after the mark had risen from 4.71 to 4.74.
causal.assumptions_right: The hike-sensitive part of the SOFR strip could still move higher from 4.71, and the three-basis-point rise confirmed that belief.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Follow-through beyond 4.74 was unknown, and a haven bid that pulls yields down was an underweighted way for a correct hike view to stall.
causal.causal_divergence: The position moved in the expected direction by three basis points and the close banked that move rather than leaving it exposed to a later haven-driven decline in yields.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the rise from 4.71 to 4.74 already in hand, holding for a larger move would have turned a confirmed thesis into an open bet on follow-through that the close did not require.
causal.future_implication: A completed rise in September 2027 SOFR should be realized, and the next pro-growth expression should move to the market that now shows the excessive defensive price.

postmortems.no_new_lesson: A three-basis-point gain that was closed on a completed mark is bounded variance around a sound process, and the process remains sound without a new rule to stay long that contract.

postmortems.expression_assessment: The US ten-year outright was the right rates instrument for a defensive stress bid and it realized the rally from 5.24 to 5.07. Once the driver was haven demand against a still-hawkish Fed, closing it avoided turning that overlay into a fresh receive at 5.04.

causal.original_belief: The long US ten-year from 5.24 in early October was a defensive slowdown expression that yields would fall if late-cycle growth cracked, with invalidation set as a further selloff driven by tighter policy and no growth break.
causal.observed_reality: The position was closed on 19 November at 5.07, and the yield has since only extended to 5.04 on a safe-haven bid even as the Fed minutes still discuss more hikes, with no growth break in this packet.
causal.assumptions_right: The assumption that the US ten-year could rally from 5.24 under stress was right, and honoring the invalidation left the book flat while the reaction function still discusses further hikes.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The growth-break channel was overweighted relative to the geopolitical haven channel that actually delivered the rally, and the oil-supply inflation impulse was underweighted as a reason that rally could stall.
causal.causal_divergence: The mark converged with the long because of a safe-haven bid in Treasuries, while the slowdown mechanism used to justify the trade did not print.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same information through the 19 November close, the correct action was still to exit at 5.07 rather than reload, because tighter policy without a growth break remained the live invalidation.
causal.future_implication: A future long in the US ten-year requires a growth or labor break that takes the Fed off further hikes, while a haven rally that coexists with hike talk stays a completed stress overlay.

postmortems.no_new_lesson: The process remains sound because the ticket carried an explicit invalidation, the close followed it, and the later move from 5.07 to 5.04 is bounded variance on a haven extension.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Long EURGBP was a clean non-dollar expression of a valuation gap, and the flat result does not spoil that choice. Spot is now through 0.8331, so the same expression is not available for re-entry.

causal.original_belief: EURGBP was cheap enough on valuation to hold a long entered at 0.83, abandoned only on a break through 0.8331 or if a UK yield premium explained the cheapness.
causal.observed_reality: The long was entered and exited at 0.83 after about one day and closed on 19 November. Spot is now 0.83581, through 0.8331, while the one-year valuation gap has not closed.
causal.assumptions_right: EURGBP was the right cross for the euro-sterling gap, and defining 0.8331 as the exit kept the ticket from being held after the level broke.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A one-day window was short relative to a one-year valuation gap, and 0.8331 sat close enough to 0.83 that ordinary noise could print the technical invalidation.
causal.causal_divergence: The flat result came from exiting at the entry price, not from the valuation gap closing. After the exit, spot traded through 0.8331 while the one-year gap stayed wide.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With only the entry information, the rule was to keep the long until 0.8331 broke. Once that level broke, the same rule is flat, which is the state now.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Short September 2027 SOFR was a weak expression of residual hike risk because the entry at 4.75 sat on the September jump, the peak did not extend it, and the contract-specific invalidation then ended the trade at 4.74.
postmortems.lesson: Do not roll a finished front SOFR short into the peak contract just to keep a hawkish story.
postmortems.future_rule: Invalidate a short-rate on that contract's own path, and do not open a new short in the peak contract merely to keep a hawkish story in the book.

causal.original_belief: The 17 September SOFR jump was the start of a further hawkish repricing, and rolling a finished front short into September 2027 would keep the book paid as the Fed held the path higher.
causal.observed_reality: The short was opened at 4.75 on 19 September and closed at 4.74 on 19 November after the nearer contract retraced the 17 September jump, a one basis point loss on a short rate.
causal.assumptions_right: The exit rule held: invalidation belonged to that contract's own path, and the position was closed when the jump was retraced.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: September 2027 was already the peak, and the September jump was already inside the 4.75 entry, so the roll preserved a story after the front expression was finished.
causal.causal_divergence: The nearer contract gave back the jump it already contained, so the implied rate fell one basis point, while the broader case for a higher policy path did not require this peak contract to keep rising.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the same information, the finished front short should have been left completed, and September 2027 should have stayed flat unless its own implied rate cheapened.
causal.future_implication: The next hawkish US view stays out of September 2027 and out of any later peak contract unless that contract's own path cheapens the residual hike.

postmortems.expression_assessment: EURGBP failed as the expression of euro value. After EURUSD and EURJPY lifted, the cross stayed pinned near 0.834 and was sold back near 0.83. Remaining statistical cheapness is not a reason to reopen it.
postmortems.lesson: A covered euro-sterling value long that stays pinned after the euro legs lift no longer has its sponsor, even if the valuation gap is still extreme and the round trip is flat.
postmortems.future_rule: Do not reopen a covered EURGBP value long unless the cross responds when the euro legs move. A CAD valuation view stays in spot when the two-year spread versus cash is not a quoted instrument.

causal.original_belief: EURGBP screened cheap enough near 0.83 that the cross itself would converge once the euro lifted against the dollar and the yen.
causal.observed_reality: Over about nine days the cross stayed pinned near 0.834 and was closed on 19 November near 0.83. Oil in this packet is not a scare, so crude did not make the cheapness fair.
causal.assumptions_right: The exit honored the pin. The entry and exit were the same price, so location did not create a loss, and the stated invalidation matched the flat result.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The trade required the cross to rise after the euro legs lifted. Those legs could move while sterling matched them, and that offset was underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: The euro lift was absorbed in the dollar and yen legs. The cross stayed pinned, so the valuation gap survived and the convergence did not.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same information, the value view should not have been placed in the euro pair that was already failing to follow the euro legs.
causal.future_implication: A pinned EURGBP is not reopened on a surviving valuation gap. The next convergence has to be a cross whose fundamental sponsor is still in the print.

postmortems.expression_assessment: The spot dollar-yen short was the right single-leg expression for a tactical yen fade and the wrong expression to reload. The close at 159.42 kept the loss rule intact, and spot at 159.97 shows the upside break has reasserted.

causal.original_belief: The failed 20-day upside break in USDJPY would normalize, so a short from 159.60 had a defined end if that break reasserted.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed at 159.42 on 19 November. The latest fixing shows USDJPY at 159.97, back through the entry, which is the upside break reasserting after the close.
causal.assumptions_right: The invalidation was observable, the position was closed rather than held into the reassertion, and the dip was small enough not to treat as a completed reversal.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The failed break was not a durable reversal condition. The still-ahead inflation prints and the dollar extension across the other majors were underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: Price dipped from 159.60 to 159.42 and then reasserted to 159.97. The mean reversion did not persist.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the information at the 159.42 close, the sound action was to close rather than add. With this morning's fixing, the sound action is to stay flat rather than re-short 159.97.
causal.future_implication: A closed yen fade that then reasserts is not a reason to fade the dollar complex or the front end while the inflation prints are still ahead.

postmortems.no_new_lesson: The path from 159.60 to 159.42 was bounded variance inside a break that reasserted to 159.97. The process remains sound because the short was closed on its invalidation rule and that close is not rewritten into a new dollar fade.

Dollar-yen at 159.97 has reclaimed 159.60, so another short there is the crowded fade rather than the unowned side.
positioning-cynic.invalidation: The stand-aside ends if the hike pay or the Canada receive ceases to be the owned side, or if dollar-yen loses 159.60 because longs are forced out.

expression_memo.rationale: The obvious tickets are already owned: the public further-hike pay, the CORRA receive, and the dollar seat's short euro plus long franc. A fresh short in dollar-yen would repeat a failed-break fade after 159.60 was reclaimed.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Dollar-yen spot was a poor crowding expression. A percentile extreme is not evidence that longs were one-sided, and the 159.42 cover monetized a dip inside the invalidation.
postmortems.lesson: A cover of the dollar-yen short from 159.60 to 159.42 does not show ownership asymmetry. The reclaim through 159.60 to 159.97 shows that short was the crowded fade.
postmortems.future_rule: Do not re-short dollar-yen on stretch after 159.60 has been reclaimed, and do not treat a spot percentile as positioning while the public hike path remains the consensus.

causal.original_belief: Dollar-yen had failed a break, and the extension looked crowded enough that a short from 159.60 would extend lower rather than reclaim that level.
causal.observed_reality: The short was covered at 159.42 on 19 November, and by this cutoff dollar-yen is 159.97, above 159.60.
causal.assumptions_right: Covering at 159.42 left the book flat before the reclaim. The invalidation was a hold above 159.60, and 159.97 now meets that test.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A stretched dollar-yen print was treated as crowded longs. The public hike story and the existing short euro and long franc were the consensus, and the dip did not show those dollar longs being forced out.
causal.causal_divergence: The fade needed the failed break to stay failed. Price reclaimed 159.60 and traded 159.97, which is continuation of the dollar bid rather than a squeeze of a one-sided long.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the same evidence the book should have stayed flat in dollar-yen. A high print and a failed-break label were not ownership.
causal.future_implication: After 159.60 is reclaimed, another dollar-yen short on stretch repeats the crowded fade. A later short needs a fresh failure back through 159.60.
